name: USA
lead: The United States stretches from the Atlantic to the Pacific. It has 50 states, with mountains, deserts, prairies, and tropical islands. Americans invented the lightbulb, the aeroplane, and the internet. About 340 million people live there.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: The USA has six time zones and almost every climate. The Rocky Mountains split the west. The Mississippi River flows south to the Gulf of Mexico.
Alaska has glaciers and the continent's tallest peak. Hawaii lies 3,800 km out in the Pacific. It is a chain of volcanoes with active lava. The Grand Canyon makes its own weather.
animals: The bald eagle has been the national symbol since 1782. Bison once numbered 60 million on the Great Plains. Hunters nearly wiped them out.
Monarch butterflies fly 4,000 km each autumn to Mexican forests. Wolves returned to Yellowstone in 1995. They kept elk moving and changed the course of rivers.
culture: American culture is a remix. Jazz began in New Orleans. Hip-hop began in New York. Billions of people watch Hollywood films. Baseball, basketball, and football fill huge stadiums.
New York has pizza, Texas has barbecue, and Louisiana has gumbo. The USA has about 17,000 public libraries, more than McDonald's restaurants.
history: American Indians lived here for 15,000 years before Europeans came. In 1776, Britain's 13 colonies declared independence. They won the Revolutionary War and launched the first modern democracy.
The country grew west. It fought a Civil War (1861–65) to end slavery. After the Cold War ended in 1991, it was the only superpower.
wows: The USA has over 1,200 tornadoes a year, more than any other country.
Alaska is just 88 km of sea from Russia.
The Library of Congress holds over 175 million items.
Yellowstone sits on a supervolcano. Its magma chamber is as big as Los Angeles.
Americans eat about 3 billion pizzas every year.
US interstate highways could circle Earth's equator nearly twice.
Over 400 Nobel Prize winners came from the USA.

myths.myth: The Statue of Liberty was made in America
myths.fact: France built it and gave it as a gift in 1886. It crossed the ocean in 350 pieces.

myths.myth: Lightning never strikes the same place twice
myths.fact: It often does. The Empire State Building gets hit about 20 times a year.
